properties.name: Bradbury Landing
properties.description: Historic touchdown site of NASA's Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity rover on August 6, 2012 in northern Gale Crater.
properties.geology: Alluvial fan gravels and basaltic regolith washed down from the northern crater rim (Peace Vallis).
properties.image_caption: Bradbury Landing viewed by Curiosity Mastcam

properties.name: Yellowknife Bay (John Klein Drill)
properties.description: Depression where Curiosity discovered evidence of an ancient freshwater lake with neutral pH, low salinity, and essential bio-elements (C, H, N, O, P, S).
properties.geology: Fine-grained Sheepbed mudstone with phyllosilicate smectite clays, calcium sulfate veins, and magnetite.
properties.image_caption: First drill hole on Mars at John Klein outcrop

properties.name: The Kimberley Outcrops
properties.description: Intersection of three distinct geological terrains showing prominent cross-bedding and high potassium concentrations (Windjana drill).
properties.geology: Feldspar-rich sanidine basalt sandstone with complex river channel migration stratification.
properties.image_caption: Cross-bedded strata at Mount Remarkable in The Kimberley

properties.name: Pahrump Hills (Murray Formation Base)
properties.description: First exposed basal strata of Mount Sharp (Aeolis Mons), marking the boundary between crater floor gravels and the 5-km-high central peak.
properties.geology: Laminated lacustrine mudstone with dendritic crystals, silica enrichments, and jarosite sulfates.

properties.name: Vera Rubin Ridge (Hematite Ridge)
properties.description: A prominent topographic ridge standing 30 meters above surrounding plains, enriched in crystalline hematite formed by ancient groundwater interaction.
properties.geology: Hardened mudstones and sandstones intensely cemented by gray hematite, resistant to wind erosion.
properties.image_caption: Panorama of Vera Rubin Ridge and Mount Sharp summit

properties.name: Glen Torridon (Clay-Bearing Trough)
properties.description: Trough south of Vera Rubin Ridge with the highest concentration of clay minerals observed from orbit by CRISM, indicating prolonged quiet lake conditions.
properties.geology: Fine-grained smectite clay phyllosilicates preserving organic molecules and cyclic lacustrine depositional rhythms.
properties.image_caption: Curiosity panorama of the clay-bearing Glen Torridon trough

properties.name: Mount Sharp Boxwork Formations (NASA 2025/2026 Target)
properties.description: A striking web of prominent mineral ridges formed when mineral-saturated warm groundwater seeped into bedrock cracks and hardened. Later wind erosion stripped away the softer rock, leaving the boxwork standing.
properties.geology: Calcium sulfate / silica mineral vein networks stretching for kilometers, providing a subterranean habitable oasis during Mars drying era.
properties.image_caption: Curiosity Mastcam-Z inspection of spiderweb-like boxwork ridges

properties.name: Layered Sulfate-Bearing Unit
properties.description: Marks the dramatic planetary climate transition when Mars lost its surface water, shifting from warm/wet lake environments to a hyper-arid desert.
properties.geology: Rippled sandstones cemented with pure magnesium and calcium sulfates, interbedded with wind-blown dune cross-beds.
properties.image_caption: Sulfate-rich layered canyon walls of lower Mount Sharp
